summary: President Donald Trump told Vice President JD Vance to focus on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-led cities and states after Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses. The instruction weakens Vance’s ability to deliver an agreement with Iran, while further military orders and Qatar’s role remain open. Democrats are projected to control both chambers in January. A federal prosecutor warned Senator Richard Blumenthal about his inquiry into White House ballroom donors, and Blumenthal sought the prosecutor’s records. House Democrats questioned their leadership’s floor preparation after the vote to send Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s impeachment resolution to committee. Nvidia’s board named Colette Kress interim chief executive after Jensen Huang resigned. Minneapolis council members voted for project-by-project review of data centers. AP called the Kansas governor’s race for Cindy Holscher. U.S. envoys continued talks with Russia and Ukraine, and an actual prisoner transfer remains unverified. Canada warned Stellantis it could sue over an auto plant funding agreement. Alaska race results, the Venezuela talks, major immigration and tariff court developments and Lisa Cook’s hearing remain open.
scope: Focused November 12–13 review of Trump’s instruction to Vance, post-election reactions, oversight, Nvidia, local zoning, election calls, Russia talks and a Canadian trade response. The latest court orders on immigration and tariffs, Iran military operations, Venezuela talks and Lisa Cook’s hearing remain unverified.

major_developments.finding: Trump pulls JD Vance away from Iran talks and directs him to focus on alleged crime and corruption at home
major_developments.reason: My reading: Trump can narrow Vance’s role in making a deal. Vance’s next assignment could keep him in front of Republican voters, while his ability to deliver a diplomatic result has weakened. A new military order or domestic enforcement program remains unverified.

major_developments.finding: Senator John Kennedy disputes JD Vance’s account of why Republicans lost the midterms
major_developments.reason: My reading: Kennedy’s criticism gives Republicans who emphasize domestic concerns an argument against Vance’s explanation. The available reporting shows disagreement among elected Republicans. Primary voter response remains unknown.

major_developments.finding: Nvidia names Colette Kress interim chief executive after Jensen Huang resigns
major_developments.reason: My reading: Huang’s departure removes a chief executive who had dealt directly with Trump. The board controls the succession, and the filing leaves the board inquiry and any security allegations unresolved.

major_developments.finding: Minneapolis City Council votes 7–6 for project-by-project review of new data centers
major_developments.reason: My reading: The vote gives council members a way to deny specific projects if the ordinance takes effect. State building rules and decisions about supplying power remain separate.

major_developments.finding: Associated Press calls Kansas governor’s race for Democrat Cindy Holscher
major_developments.reason: My reading: Kansas Republicans still face a Democratic governor who can veto legislation. This call concerns the state executive branch and leaves federal chamber totals where they were.

major_developments.finding: Senator Richard Blumenthal asks U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz to preserve records about the White House ballroom inquiry
major_developments.reason: My reading: The exchange exposes the prosecutor’s role to congressional scrutiny. Preservation can protect records for later demands. Whether either side obtains the documents or takes compulsory action remains open.

major_developments.finding: Democrats Delia Ramirez and Melat Kiros question House leaders’ preparation after the Hegseth vote
major_developments.reason: My reading: Members who want more influence over floor planning can use the losses to press their case. Jeffries’s example shows the party could still organize a vote on another issue. January scheduling and support for articles remain open.

major_developments.finding: U.S. envoys meet Putin and Zelenskyy after the Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange talks
major_developments.reason: My reading: Bringing European representatives into the talks could give governments that might help defend Ukraine a say in the terms. Putin’s opposition to European troops leaves a ceasefire unresolved. The announced prisoner deal still awaits a verified transfer.

major_developments.finding: Canada gives Stellantis 30 days to address alleged breaches of its Brampton auto plant funding agreement
major_developments.reason: My reading: Canada can use the funding agreement to seek repayment or a remedy as manufacturers adjust production. The notice leaves both a lawsuit and repayment open.
